limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

findings.text: 仓库维护者和编码Agent复用架构/源索引、查证变更影响；需求强度与相对手写文档收益待核，见[Q01](#research-q01)。
Tauri App/CLI→Rust扫描/生成/分层freshness；DeepWiki真实Ask→模型Runner与检索工具→回答/引用/UI，见[Q01](#research-q01)至[Q03](#research-q03)。

统计仅Markdown/TS/JS/MJS列项，未计核心Rust与Svelte，不代表全工程代码量，不补造数量。固定材料摘要/身份版本已核；当前根对象无正式旧研究。检查真实Tauri/前端消费者、生成dispatch/文件判据、分层freshness/预载、Ask/FunctionTool/citation/自动写与env执行。未运行/装包/调用模型、未全审所有SDD/外部SDK内部循环、目录权限/下载脱敏/平台退出或安全。
Rust workspace与Tauri应用0.9.8，私有前端package0.9.7；外部Agent/Skill/工具各有版本，未验证线上发行物/统一兼容。固定提交日期非发布日期。
成品/CLI、可读写项目目录/磁盘，Git为漂移/基线/相应增量条件，与所选ACP/native后端、按需Skill/工具各自约束；完整四列表见[Q04](#research-q04)。
首次固定版本/副本与后端；持续/Ask生成有资源，失败部分安装和全量清旧需保全，退出撤规则/工具按差异处理；现金/人工四阶段表见[Q04](#research-q04)。
复制允许处理的仓库，先生成少量知识并核源码定位/更新；明确接受Ask准备写入及模型路由，环境安装另按选择评估，见[Q04](#research-q04)、[Q05](#research-q05)。
已有完整性/同步/指标和引文返回能使资料状态可见，不等事实正确或已节时；四项效果表见[Q02](#research-q02)。
保留缺基线降信任、文档集/最低结构报错、事件与部分错误可见；同步启发式和未知预载/输入树边界须单独核，不许文档数量当结果，见[Q02](#research-q02)。
仓库资料共址、增量/skip和分层漂移信任、GUI与真实检索工具组合；独立能力主表、步骤见Q01，结果边界见[Q02](#research-q02)。
完整/新鲜不等语义正确；无freshness和ledger时预载默许，Ask可写知识/调模型，Hybrid异常fallback不证明未写，见[Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)。
超出现有Git分层指标与正则引用，检验固定树的关键架构命题和变更反证；独立任务/指标/停止条件见[Q05](#research-q05)。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)既有知识/模型/工具组合novelty25%超纯列表0%，非新算法阻50%；[Q02](#research-q02)/[Q03](#research-q03)真实生成、分层可信/自动准备与消费mechanism75%超孤立同步50%，未知预载/语义与外部后端未闭合阻100%；core/CLI/GUI共享能力transfer50%超只单UI25%，运行生态依赖阻75%；增量/skip/统一资料simplification50%超手配25%，实际维护/语义核查负担阻75%。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)到[Q03](#research-q03)资料生成/查询/状态workflow50%超孤立文档25%，用户交付/准确对照阻75%；独立桌面与CLI/选定工具集成delivery/reach50%超单内部脚本25%，成品/跨Agent真实采用未核阻75%；[Q02](#research-q02)差异更新/skip有避免重复生成的economics25%超无资源机制0%，无总费/工时净益实测阻50%。

recommendation.reason: 维护代码仓库并明确允许知识资产写入与所选模型调用的开发者，可在复制仓库中用 Terrain 组织架构资料、查看Git漂移并向源码追查问题。相比手写约定与反复grep，源码支持共用知识入口、增量准备和真实工具检索，但文档完整与Freshness绿态不能代替架构事实及最终任务验收。若引用或判断与源码冲突、自动准备超出允许范围或部分环境安装难以撤回，应暂停生成与安装，保留文件差异和已有资料，退回原仓的文档与编辑器流程。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)维护/架构定位50%超泛Agent25%，频率/真实用户需求阻75%。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)增量/分层与[Q03](#research-q03)真实工具共用50%超资料列表25%，语义价值未证阻75%。

evidence.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)至[Q04](#research-q04)真实UI/命令/callee/失败50%超README25%，无运行/正确率阻75%，不把源码链当成品质量。

cost.rationale: [Q04](#research-q04)副本/按选项/跳过与部分错误可见50%超必须全局安装25%，模型/自动写/卸载恢复未知阻75%。

publication.summaries.text: 独立桌面与CLI将仓库知识、Agent工具和Git漂移组织到一起；文档完整、资料同步和回答正确是不同判据，Ask还可自动准备并写知识资产。

items.界面: Tauri/Svelte知识生成、状态和真实DeepWiki消费
items.模型工具: native Ask的search/read/pack工具，read context可确保并生成资产
items.Skill: 按需部署外部/预设约定，非每项已审或DSH根bundle

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|
| 仓库scan/pack | 生成源码索引/项目材料 | feature/同步状态影响是否打包，不等全产品离线 |
| Human知识生成 | 产出架构/深探索文档 | ACP/native及Skill，full会清旧，文件集完整不等正确 |
| Agent context更新 | 增量或全量维护上下文 | 最低结构/字数与基线，不是事实验收 |
| Freshness | 显示分层Git漂移/年龄信任 | 启发式分数，未知预载分支另核 |
| DeepWiki Ask | 将问题交模型与工具并回回答 | 缺/旧资产可先写/生成，建engine失败搜索降级 |
| search_knowledge | 搜文档并回JSON | 实际KnowledgeSearch，命中不证明回答事实 |
| read_doc/pack grep/read | 为模型读取文档/源码包片段 | 版本/路径/引用仍需对真实仓复核 |
| read_agent_context | 按节读上下文 | ensure_ready可能生成，不能统称纯读 |
| 来源引用 | 返回路径/行及可查看来源 | 正则解析不等存在/语义已核 |
| 环境apply | 部署选定工具/Skill/约定 | 命令真实执行、可部分失败，非全量事务/卸载保证 |

publication.advice.text: 复制允许处理的仓库，先生成少量知识并核源码定位/更新；明确接受Ask准备写入及模型路由，环境安装另按选择评估，见[Q04](#research-q04)、[Q05](#research-q05)。

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "<div align=\"center\">\n    <img height=\"320\" src=\"./assets/banner.webp\">\n\n# Terrain\n\n**Terrain prepares the ground so agents don't have to guess where to stand.**\n\nEngineering environment management for human developers and AI coding assistants — knowledge as the map, tools as the roads, conventions as the trail markers.\n\n**English** · [简体中文](README_zh.md)\n\n<a href=\"https://github.com/sopaco/terrain/tree/dev/.terrain/human\"><img alt=\"Litho Docs\" src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/Litho-Docs-green?logo=Gitbook&color=%23008a60\"/></a>\n![Agent Ready](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agent-READY-green.svg)\n![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)\n\n</div>\n\n---\n\n## App preview\n\n| Project overview | Engineering knowledge | DeepWiki Q&A | Agent environment |\n|------------------|------------------------------|--------------|-------------------|\n| <img height=\"150\" alt=\"image\" src=\"assets/screenshots/01-overview.webp\" /> | <img height=\"150\" alt=\"Auto-generated C4 architecture docs\" src=\"assets/screenshots/02-knowledge-litho.webp\"> | <img height=\"150\" alt=\"Knowledge-grounded Q&A with citations\" src=\"assets/screenshots/03-deepwiki-ask.webp\"> | <img height=\"150\" alt=\"One-command agent tooling setup\" src=\"assets/screenshots/05-env.png\"> |\n\n*From left to right: project list with freshness scores, auto-generated C4 docs, knowledge-grounded Q&A, and one-command agent tooling setup.*\n\n---\n\n## Contents\n\n- [What is Terrain?](#what-is-terrain)\n- [Install](#install)\n- [Getting started](#getting-started)\n- [CLI command reference](#cli-command-reference)\n- [Why Terrain?](#why-terrain)\n- [Architecture](#architecture)\n- [Ecosystem](#ecosystem)\n- [From Litho to Terrain](#from-litho-to-terrain)\n- [License](#license)\n\n---\n\n## What is Terrain?\n\nTerrain is a **standardized, AI-friendly engineering environment**. Point it at a Git repository and it delivers three things:\n\n![terrain_caseflow](./assets/intro/terrain_caseflow_en.webp)\n\n- **🗺️ Engineering knowledge** — always-in-sync C4 docs and agent context, **produced from your code and consumed by both humans and AI agents**.\n- **🤝 A shared agent contract** — Skills, `AGENTS.md`, and CLIs, so every coding agent reads the project the same way instead of blind-grepping the live repo.\n- **⚙️ Auto-deployed tooling** — one command installs what your agents need (CodeGraph, RTK, preset Skills); no per-repo yak-shaving.\n\nIt runs as a **desktop app (GUI)** or a **CLI** — see [Getting started](#getting-started) for which to pick.\n\n### Three pillars\n\n| Pillar | Metaphor | What you get |\n|--------|----------|--------------|\n| **Knowledge assets** | *Map* | Dual-track docs in `.terrain/`, produced from code |\n| **Agent tooling** | *Roads* | CodeGraph, RTK, and the Terrain CLI |\n| **Conventions & workflow** | *Trail markers* | Skills, `AGENTS.md`, and the four-phase SDD workflow |\n\nOne codebase, two audiences:\n\n| Audience | Path | Format |\n|----------|------|--------|\n| **Humans** | `.terrain/human/` | Narrative C4 docs with Mermaid diagrams |\n| **AI agents** | `.terrain/agent/context.md` | Structured architecture overview (≤ 14 KiB) |\n| **Source index** | `.terrain/agent/repomix.md` | Repomix pack — grep/read on demand, not preloaded |\n| **Domain terms** | `.terrain/knowledge/` | Business glossary and internal conventions |\n\n### Knowledge factory\n\n<img height=\"360\" src=\"./assets/graph_knowledge_factory.webp\">\n\n### Why it stands out\n\n- **Incremental** — tracks Git HEAD and regenerates only what changed, not the whole knowledge base.\n- **Freshness-scored** — every asset carries a score; agents down-weight context below 50.\n- **One contract for every agent** — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Cursor read the same layers through `terrain tools`.\n- **Toolchain in one command** — `terrain env apply` installs CodeGraph, RTK, and preset Skills in dependency order.\n- **Reviewable workflow** — SDD turns requirements → design → codegen → review into Markdown artifacts.\n\n### Performance & integration\n\n- **Native Rust core** — a single binary, no runtime, no database. Scan, pack, search, freshness, and env run fully offline with no LLM call.\n- **Cross-platform** — prebuilt desktop installers for macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows x64, plus `@terrain-ai/cli` on npm for headless machines and CI.\n- **Pipeline-friendly** — JSON stdout on every `terrain tools` call and NDJSON event streaming from `terrain ask query --stream`, so Terrain drops into CI jobs, PR checks, and agent loops without glue code.\n\n---\n\n## Install\n\n### Option 1 — Prebuilt installer (recommended)\n\nDownload the package for your platform from [**GitHub Releases**](https://github.com/sopaco/terrain/releases) and open it — no Rust or Node toolchain required.\n\n| Platform | Asset |\n|----------|-------|\n| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `Terrain_<version>_macos_aarch64.dmg` |\n| Windows (x64) | `Terrain_<version>_windows_x64.exe` |\n\n> **Unsigned builds — first-launch notice.** The installers are not yet signed with an Apple Developer ID / Authenticode certificate, so both platforms raise a one-time warning. The download is intact; see below to continue.\n\n#### macOS — \"Terrain is damaged / should be moved to the Trash\"\n\nThis is Gatekeeper, not a corrupt file. Downloads from the internet carry a `com.apple.quarantine` attribute, and macOS refuses to launch an unsigned app with that flag set. Remove the flag after copying `Terrain.app` to `/Applications`:\n\n```bash\nxattr -cr /Applications/Terrain.app\n```\n\n#### Windows — SmartScreen \"Windows protected your PC\"\n\nClick **More info → Run anyway**. The prompt appears once per build.\n\n### Option 2 — Build from source\n\nUse this path for unsupported platforms, custom patches, or contributing to Terrain itself.\n\n#### Prerequisites\n\n- **Rust** — stable toolchain (MSRV 1.94; see [rust-toolchain.toml](rust-toolchain.toml))\n- **Node.js / Bun** — frontend toolchain and optional Node-based tools\n- **LLM access** (optional) — OpenAI-compatible API, Ollama, or LM Studio (configure in the desktop app **Settings** panel)\n- **Mainstream coding agent** (optional) — e.g. Codex, DeepSeek Harness, or Claude Code, for knowledge composition and SDD codegen\n\n#### Build\n\n```bash\n# Clone and install frontend dependencies\ngit clone https://github.com/sopaco/terrain.git\ncd terrain\nbun install\n\n# Build Rust workspace (CLI + libraries)\ncargo build --release\n\n# CLI binary\n./target/release/terrain --help\n\n# Desktop app (development)\nbun run dev:app\n```\n\n---\n\n## Getting started\n\n### Which entry point should I use?\n\n| | Desktop app (GUI) | CLI |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Best for** | Day-to-day exploration and documentation of a codebase | R&D infrastructure, CI/CD, headless servers, agent pipelines |\n| **What you get** | Everything pre-wired: project list, freshness scores, C4 docs, Q&A, env setup, SDD | 15 scriptable subcommands with JSON output for automation |\n| **Requires** | Nothing beyond an optional LLM endpoint | No display; install via npm or let env integration deploy it |\n| **Typical use** | Click through the app | `terrain init`, `terrain ask query`, `terrain tools …` inside a pipeline |\n\n### Path A — Desktop app (start here)\n\nThe app bundles the full loop, so there is nothing to compose yourself.\n\n1. **Install and open** Terrain (see [Install](#install)).\n2. **Add a project** — point Terrain at a local Git repository.\n3. **Run initialization** — Terrain scans the repo, generates the six C4 docs, and writes `.terrain/`.\n4. **Read or ask** — browse the generated docs in the built-in reader, or ask a question in DeepWiki Q&A and get answers with citations.\n5. **Wire up your agents** — one click in the *Agent environment* screen installs Skills, CodeGraph, RTK, and the managed `AGENTS.md` snippets.\n\n> The CLI is included: env integration deploys it to `~/.terrain/bin/terrain`, so you can drop to the terminal at any point without a separate install.\n\n### Path B — CLI (infrastructure, CI, agent pipelines)\n\nFor headless machines, install the CLI from npm:\n\n```bash\nnpm install -g @terrain-ai/cli   # or: bunx @terrain-ai/cli <command>\n```\n\nThen drive the same knowledge pipeline from a script or pipeline:\n\n```bash\n# 1. Register a repository\nterrain assets register ./my-repo --slug my-repo\n\n# 2. Full initialization: scan + C4 docs + agent context\nterrain init ./my-repo\n\n# 3. Ask the knowledge base\nterrain ask query \"How does authentication flow through this project?\" --project my-repo\n\n# 4. Cheap refresh after commits (skips doc regeneration)\nterrain refresh ./my-repo\n```\n\nTypical CI usage — regenerate knowledge on merge, then report freshness in the job log:\n\n```bash\nterrain refresh .\nterrain project freshness-cached --project my-repo\n```\n\nExternal agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor) pull the same knowledge through the JSON API:\n\n```bash\nterrain tools list-projects\nterrain tools read-context --project my-repo\nterrain tools grep-pack --project my-repo --pattern \"authenticate\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## CLI command reference\n\nThe commands you will reach for most. Every command accepts a global `--repo-path` override.\n\n### Knowledge assets\n\n| Command | Purpose |\n|---------|---------|\n| `terrain assets register <path> --slug <slug>` | Register a repository with the local registry |\n| `terrain init [path]` | Full initialization — scan + C4 docs + agent context |\n| `terrain refresh [path]` | Quick refresh — scan + repack + context, skips doc generation |\n| `terrain ask query <query> --project <slug>` | Natural-language Q&A over the knowledge base (`--stream` for NDJSON) |\n| `terrain search <query>` | Full-text search across generated knowledge |\n| `terrain project overview --project <slug>` | Freshness scores, doc counts, and paths |\n\n### Environment standardization\n\n| Command | Purpose |\n|---------|---------|\n| `terrain env status` | Check which Skills, tools, and `AGENTS.md` snippets are installed |\n| `terrain env plan` | Preview what `apply` would change |\n| `terrain env apply` | Install Skills, CodeGraph, RTK, and `AGENTS.md` in dependency order |\n| `terrain tools <command> --project <slug>` | JSON API for external agents — `read-context`, `search`, `read-doc`, `grep-pack`, `freshness` |\n\n**Full CLI guide:** [Terrain CLI Guides](.terrain/human/5.Boundaries-Interfaces.md) — all 15 subcommands, including SDD (`sdd run`), token usage (`usage`), and pipeline internals (`assets …`).\n\n---\n\n## Why Terrain?\n\nOnboarding to a new codebase usually means days of reading source and stale wiki pages. Terrain compresses that to minutes: register a repo, run initialization, and get a full C4 doc set plus an agent-ready context pack.\n\n| Without Terrain | With Terrain |\n|------------------|---------------|\n| Architecture knowledge scattered across wikis, Slack, and senior engineers | Engineering knowledge assets generated from the actual codebase |\n| AI assistants grep the live repo blindly | Agents read `context.md` first, then targeted repomix slices |\n| Docs drift from code on every refactor | Incremental updates + freshness tracking; knowledge travels with Git branches |\n| Every team reinvents \"how to onboard an AI to our repo\" | Env integration installs Skills, CodeGraph, RTK, and `AGENTS.md` snippets |\n\n**Built for:**\n\n- **Developers** exploring or documenting a codebase\n- **Tech leads** who want architecture docs that stay close to the code\n- **Teams** adopting AI coding assistants and need a shared knowledge contract\n- **CI/CD** pipelines that regenerate knowledge assets on merge\n- **ACP integrators** wiring `terrain tools` into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or compatible agents\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n### System overview\n\n![terrain_caseflow](./assets/intro/terrain_caseflow_en.webp)\n\nHumans use the **desktop app** or **CLI**; external coding agents use the same contract via **`terrain tools`** (JSON stdout). Assets live **in-repo** (`.terrain/` travels with branches); `~/.terrain/registry.json` holds project pointers only.\n\n### ① Knowledge assets — the map\n\nDual-track output from one factory — narrative `human/` for people, structured `agent/` for machines.\n\n**Produce** (scan/pack run offline; LLM/ACP where noted):\n\n```\nGit ──scan──► index.md\n    ──pack──► repomix.md\n    ──context (LLM)──► context.md\n    ──docs (ACP)──► human/ + .litho-agent/ checkpoints\n    ──track──► freshness.json\n```\n\n**Consume** — DeepWiki and `terrain tools` share the same three layers:\n\n| Layer | Source | API |\n|-------|--------|-----|\n| Macro | `agent/context.md` | `read-context` |\n| Meso | `human/`, `knowledge/` | `search`, `read-doc` |\n| Micro | `agent/repomix.md` | `grep-pack` → `read-pack-file` |\n\nWhen sources conflict: **repomix > CodeGraph > context.md > human/**. Down-weight macro context when `freshness_score < 50`.\n\n### ② Agent tooling — the roads\n\n`terrain env apply` installs the navigation layer so agents don't improvise:\n\n| Component | Purpose |\n|-----------|---------|\n| **Tools** | `~/.terrain/bin/` — CodeGraph, RTK, `terrain` CLI (`terrain tools` for ACP) |\n| **Skills** | Standard playbooks — terrain-knowledge → repomix → codegraph → rtk |\n| **AGENTS.md** | Managed snippets — knowledge-first workflow, repomix for code, RTK for shell |\n\n### ③ Conventions & workflow — the trail markers\n\nSDD defines a repeatable path; each phase produces a reviewable Markdown artifact:\n\n| Phase | Output | Engine |\n|-------|--------|--------|\n| Requirements | `1.requirements.md` | Native LLM |\n| Tech design | `2.tech-design.md` | Native LLM |\n| Codegen | `3.implementation.md` + repo changes | ACP agent |\n| Code review | `4.code-review.md` | Native LLM |\n\n```bash\nterrain sdd run --project my-repo --phase requirements\n```\n\nSession outputs live under `~/.terrain/sdd/{project}/sessions/{id}/outputs/` (local, not versioned). The knowledge pipeline uses the same resumable pattern — research checkpoints under `.terrain/.litho-agent/`.\n\n### Runtime\n\n```mermaid\ngraph LR\n    Chan[Desktop · CLI] --> Intel[terrain-agent]\n    Chan --> Core[terrain-core]\n    Intel --> Core\n    Intel --> LLM[LLM]\n    Intel --> ACP[ACP]\n    Core --> FS[\".terrain/ · Git · registry\"]\n```\n\nCore handles scan, pack, search, freshness, and env without an LLM. Agent orchestrates DeepWiki, knowledge generation, SDD, and context generation — lightweight tasks via native LLM, heavy tool-using work via ACP subprocess.\n\n### `.terrain/` directory (per project)\n\n```\n{your-repo}/.terrain/\n├── index.md                 # Project index (from scan)\n├── agent/\n│   ├── context.md           # Macro architecture context for agents\n│   ├── repomix.md           # Source pack (generated, often gitignored)\n│   └── meta.json            # Pack metadata\n├── human/                   # Engineering knowledge docs (1.Overview.md, 2.Architecture.md, …)\n├── knowledge/               # Domain glossary and conventions\n├── .meta/\n│   ├── sync.json            # Scan sync state\n│   └── freshness.json       # Asset freshness scores\n└── .litho-agent/            # Litho/knowledge research workspace (transient)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Ecosystem\n\nTerrain composes with the tools your AI workflow already uses:\n\n| Component | Role |\n|-----------|------|\n| **Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / ACP agents** | Execute knowledge composition, SDD codegen, and tool calls in an isolated process |\n| **Repomix** | Packs source into a grep-friendly index for agents |\n| **CodeGraph** | Symbol callers/callees/impact queries via `bunx codegraph` |\n| **RTK** | Compresses shell output to save tokens (`@terrain-ai/rtk` on npm, or `~/.terrain/bin/rtk`) |\n| **Terrain CLI** | Scan, assets, `terrain tools` for ACP (`@terrain-ai/cli` on npm, or `~/.terrain/bin/terrain`) |\n| **Preset Skills** | LLM workflow instructions in `preset_skills/` (knowledge, SDD, Ask, Context) |\n| **DeepWiki / Litho Book** | Knowledge-grounded Q&A and Markdown reader, integrated in the desktop UI |\n\nTrust model for coding agents: when sources conflict, **repomix source > CodeGraph > context.md > human docs**.\n\n---\n\n## From Litho to Terrain\n\nTerrain's knowledge engine is the direct successor of **Litho**, the AI documentation generator published as [deepwiki-rs](https://github.com/sopaco/deepwiki-rs) (**1.7k★**). Litho proved the core thesis at scale — *generate architecture docs from code, keep them in sync, make them agent-ready*. Terrain takes that practice and hardens it into a platform: incremental updates instead of full regeneration, broad language and framework adaptation, ACP access for external agents, and the Litho Book reader and Q&A built into the desktop app.\n\nIn short: if you liked Litho for docs, Terrain is Litho's knowledge core **plus** the environment, workflow, and agent bridge around it.\n\n---\n\n## License\n\nMIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).\n"

      "path": "crates/terrain-agent/src/agent_assets.rs",
      "content": "use std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse terrain_core::{\n    agent_context_synced_with_head, agent_pack_synced_with_head, maybe_pack_agent_assets,\n    resolve_project_repo_path, KnowledgePaths,\n};\n\nuse crate::acp::{execution_uses_native_llm, resolve_acp_settings};\nuse crate::settings::resolve_knowledge_settings;\nuse crate::agent_context::run_agent_context_generation;\nuse crate::chat::{ChatEngine, ChatPhase};\nuse crate::model::ModelConfig;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, serde::Serialize)]\npub struct AgentAssetsEnsureReport {\n    pub packed: bool,\n    pub context_generated: bool,\n}\n\n/// Pack repomix when missing. Returns true if a new pack was written.\npub async fn ensure_agent_pack(\n    paths: &KnowledgePaths,\n    project_slug: &str,\n    repo_path_hint: Option<&str>,\n) -> anyhow::Result<(String, bool)> {\n    let repo_path = resolve_project_repo_path(paths, project_slug, repo_path_hint)?;\n    if agent_pack_synced_with_head(paths, project_slug, &repo_path) {\n        return Ok((repo_path, false));\n    }\n    tracing::info!(\n        project = project_slug,\n        repo = %repo_path,\n        \"agent repomix pack missing or stale — packing automatically\"\n    );\n    maybe_pack_agent_assets(paths, project_slug, &repo_path).await?;\n    Ok((repo_path, true))\n}\n\n/// Generate context.md when missing or baseline drifted (repomix must already exist).\npub async fn generate_agent_context_if_missing(\n    paths: &KnowledgePaths,\n    model_config: &ModelConfig,\n    project_slug: &str,\n    repo_path: &str,\n) -> anyhow::Result<bool> {\n    if agent_context_synced_with_head(paths, project_slug, repo_path) {\n        return Ok(false);\n    }\n    tracing::info!(\n        project = project_slug,\n        \"agent context missing or stale — generating automatically\"\n    );\n    let acp = resolve_acp_settings();\n    let engine = if execution_uses_native_llm(&acp) {\n        Some(Arc::new(ChatEngine::new_native(paths.clone(), model_config.clone())?))\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n    run_agent_context_generation(\n        paths,\n        engine,\n        &acp,\n        project_slug,\n        repo_path,\n        &resolve_knowledge_settings(),\n        false,\n    )\n    .await?;\n    Ok(true)\n}\n\n/// Ensure repomix pack and agent/context.md exist; run generation when missing.\npub async fn ensure_agent_assets(\n    paths: &KnowledgePaths,\n    model_config: &ModelConfig,\n    project_slug: &str,\n    repo_path_hint: Option<&str>,\n) -> anyhow::Result<AgentAssetsEnsureReport> {\n    let (repo_path, packed) = ensure_agent_pack(paths, project_slug, repo_path_hint).await?;\n    let context_generated =\n        generate_agent_context_if_missing(paths, model_config, project_slug, &repo_path).await?;\n    Ok(AgentAssetsEnsureReport {\n        packed,\n        context_generated,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Prepare agent assets before an Ask turn (pack + context). Skipped for `agent-ctx-*` sessions.\npub async fn prepare_agent_assets_for_ask(\n    paths: &KnowledgePaths,\n    model_config: &ModelConfig,\n    project_slug: &str,\n    repo_path_hint: Option<&str>,\n    mut on_phase: impl FnMut(ChatPhase),\n) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    let repo_path = resolve_project_repo_path(paths, project_slug, repo_path_hint)?;\n\n    if !agent_pack_synced_with_head(paths, project_slug, &repo_path) {\n        on_phase(ChatPhase::PreparingPack);\n        ensure_agent_pack(paths, project_slug, repo_path_hint).await?;\n    }\n\n    if !agent_context_synced_with_head(paths, project_slug, &repo_path) {\n        on_phase(ChatPhase::PreparingContext);\n        generate_agent_context_if_missing(paths, model_config, project_slug, &repo_path).await?;\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n"

Freshness score computation helpers.\n\nuse chrono::{DateTime, Utc};\n\nuse super::git::{DriftBasis, GitDrift};\nuse super::FRESH_THRESHOLD;\n\n/// Commit drift penalty per commit behind baseline (capped).\npub(crate) const COMMITS_PENALTY_PER: i32 = 2;\npub(crate) const COMMITS_PENALTY_CAP: i32 = 40;\n\n/// Changed-file ratio penalty cap.\npub(crate) const FILES_PENALTY_CAP: i32 = 30;\n\n/// Calendar age since last asset sync — light penalty so stale packs are not over-penalized.\npub(crate) const SYNC_AGE_PENALTY_PER_DAY: i32 = 1;\npub(crate) const SYNC_AGE_PENALTY_CAP: i32 = 5;\n\n/// Uncommitted source changes in the working tree.\npub(crate) const DIRTY_TREE_PENALTY: i32 = 5;\n\n/// Deducted when drift could not be measured at all — an unreachable baseline commit, or an\n/// asset that records no baseline inside a Git repo.\n///\n/// We cannot tell whether the code moved, so the layer is scored as if it had drifted as far\n/// as the measurable penalties allow (commits + files + age). That lands it below\n/// [`FRESH_THRESHOLD`] and below `MACRO_PRELOAD_THRESHOLD`, so preloaded macro context is\n/// withheld until the assets are regenerated against a reachable commit.\npub(crate) const UNMEASURED_DRIFT_PENALTY: i32 =\n    COMMITS_PENALTY_CAP + FILES_PENALTY_CAP + SYNC_AGE_PENALTY_CAP;\n\n/// `None` days-since-sync is unknown, not \"today\": charge the saturated age penalty.\nconst UNKNOWN_AGE_DAYS: u32 = SYNC_AGE_PENALTY_CAP as u32;\n\n/// `agent/context.md` is an LLM-generated derivative of the source pack, so its score is\n/// discounted — the architecture layer never claims to be as trustworthy as raw source.\n/// Consequence: this layer caps at 90, and so does the overall (minimum) score.\npub(crate) const CONTEXT_DISCOUNT: f32 = 0.9;\n\n/// Discounted context score before the source-index ceiling is applied.\npub(crate) fn discount_context_score(raw: u8) -> u8 {\n    ((raw as f32) * CONTEXT_DISCOUNT) as u8\n}\n\n/// Final context score: discounted raw score, never above the source index it derives from.\npub(crate) fn context_score_from_raw(raw: u8, pack_score: u8) -> u8 {\n    discount_context_score(raw).min(pack_score)\n}\n\n/// Score one asset layer from its drift and sync age.\n///\n/// The single fail-closed entry point for scoring. It exists so the two ways an asset can look\n/// fresh precisely because it cannot be checked — unmeasurable drift, and an unparseable sync\n/// timestamp — are decided in one place rather than at each call site:\n///\n/// - a non-measured [`GitDrift`] is never read as \"in sync\";\n/// - `days_since_sync: None` is charged the full age cap rather than counting as 0 days.\npub(crate) fn score_layer(\n    drift: &GitDrift,\n    days_since_sync: Option<u32>,\n    total_tracked_estimate: u32,\n    working_tree_dirty: bool,\n) -> u8 {\n    if !drift.is_measured() {\n        let mut score = 100 - UNMEASURED_DRIFT_PENALTY;\n        if working_tree_dirty {\n            score -= DIRTY_TREE_PENALTY;\n        }\n        return score.clamp(0, 100) as u8;\n    }\n    score_asset(\n        drift.commits_since_baseline,\n        drift.changed_files.len() as u32,\n        total_tracked_estimate,\n        days_since_sync.unwrap_or(UNKNOWN_AGE_DAYS),\n        working_tree_dirty,\n    )\n}\n\n/// Compute asset freshness score (0–100) from measured drift counts.\npub fn score_asset(\n    commits_since: u32,\n    changed_files_count: u32,\n    total_tracked_estimate: u32,\n    days_since_sync: u32,\n    working_tree_dirty: bool,\n) -> u8 {\n    let mut score: i32 = 100;\n    score -= (commits_since as i32 * COMMITS_PENALTY_PER).min(COMMITS_PENALTY_CAP);\n    if total_tracked_estimate > 0 {\n        let ratio = (changed_files_count as f64 / total_tracked_estimate as f64).min(1.0);\n        score -= (ratio * FILES_PENALTY_CAP as f64).round() as i32;\n    } else if changed_files_count > 0 {\n        score -= (changed_files_count as i32).min(FILES_PENALTY_CAP);\n    }\n    score -= (days_since_sync as i32 * SYNC_AGE_PENALTY_PER_DAY).min(SYNC_AGE_PENALTY_CAP);\n    if working_tree_dirty {\n        score -= DIRTY_TREE_PENALTY;\n    }\n    score.clamp(0, 100) as u8\n}\n\n/// Days since an RFC 3339 timestamp, or `None` when it is missing or malformed.\n///\n/// `None` means \"unknown\" and must never be read as \"synced today\" — otherwise a corrupted or\n/// absent timestamp silently buys the asset a full score.\npub(crate) fn days_since_rfc3339(value: &str) -> Option<u32> {\n    DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(value).ok().map(|dt| {\n        let now = Utc::now();\n        let synced = dt.with_timezone(&Utc);\n        now.signed_duration_since(synced).num_days().max(0) as u32\n    })\n}\n\n/// Why a layer is stale, if it is.\n///\n/// An unmeasurable drift basis is reported first and unconditionally: it is a reason to distrust\n/// the asset regardless of the score, so it must not fall through to the generic causes below.\npub(crate) fn stale_reason_for(\n    score: u8,\n    commits: u32,\n    dirty: bool,\n    ready: bool,\n    basis: DriftBasis,\n) -> Option<String> {\n    if !ready {\n        return Some(\"asset_not_ready\".into());\n    }\n    if let Some(reason) = basis.stale_reason() {\n        return Some(reason.to_string());\n    }\n    if score >= FRESH_THRESHOLD {\n        return None;\n    }\n    if commits > 0 {\n        return Some(format!(\"repo_advanced_{commits}_commits\"));\n    }\n    if dirty {\n        return Some(\"working_tree_dirty\".into());\n    }\n    Some(\"sync_age\".into())\n}\n\n/// Overall freshness is the minimum across all three asset layers (including 0 = not ready).\npub(crate) fn overall_freshness_score(pack_score: u8, ctx_score: u8, human_score: u8) -> u8 {\n    [pack_score, ctx_score, human_score]\n        .into_iter()\n        .min()\n        .unwrap_or(0)\n}\n\npub(crate) fn short_git_ref(value: Option<&str>) -> Option<String> {\n    value.map(|h| {\n        let h = h.trim();\n        if h.len() <= 7 {\n            h.to_string()\n        } else {\n            h.chars().take(7).collect()\n        }\n    })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::freshness::{FRESH_THRESHOLD, MACRO_PRELOAD_THRESHOLD};\n\n    #[test]\n    fn overall_score_includes_not_ready_layers() {\n        assert_eq!(overall_freshness_score(100, 0, 100), 0);\n        assert_eq!(overall_freshness_score(0, 100, 100), 0);\n        assert_eq!(overall_freshness_score(100, 80, 100), 80);\n        assert_eq!(overall_freshness_score(50, 60, 70), 50);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn sync_age_penalty_capped_at_five() {\n        assert_eq!(score_asset(0, 0, 100, 0, false), 100);\n        assert_eq!(score_asset(0, 0, 100, 3, false), 97);\n        assert_eq!(score_asset(0, 0, 100, 7, false), 95);\n        assert_eq!(score_asset(0, 0, 100, 30, false), 95);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn score_decreases_with_commits_and_age() {\n        let fresh = score_asset(0, 0, 100, 0, false);\n        assert!(fresh >= 95);\n\n        let stale = score_asset(25, 50, 100, 10, true);\n        assert!(stale < FRESH_THRESHOLD);\n        assert!(stale < MACRO_PRELOAD_THRESHOLD);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn unmeasured_drift_is_scored_as_stale() {\n        use crate::freshness::git::{DriftBasis, GitDrift};\n\n        for basis in [DriftBasis::BaselineUnreachable, DriftBasis::BaselineMissing] {\n            let drift = GitDrift::unmeasured(basis);\n            assert!(!drift.is_measured(), \"{basis:?}\");\n\n            let score = score_layer(&drift, Some(0), 24, false);\n            assert_eq!(score, 25, \"{basis:?}\");\n            // Unmeasurable drift must withhold preloaded macro context, not merely warn.\n            assert!(score < MACRO_PRELOAD_THRESHOLD, \"{basis:?}\");\n            assert!(score < FRESH_THRESHOLD, \"{basis:?}\");\n            // A dirty tree costs the same 5 points as everywhere else.\n            assert_eq!(score_layer(&drift, Some(0), 24, true), 20, \"{basis:?}\");\n\n            assert_eq!(\n                stale_reason_for(score, 0, false, true, basis).as_deref(),\n                basis.stale_reason()\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn measured_zero_drift_still_earns_full_marks() {\n        use crate::freshness::git::{DriftBasis, GitDrift};\n\n        let drift = GitDrift {\n            commits_since_baseline: 0,\n            changed_files: vec![],\n            basis: DriftBasis::Measured,\n        };\n        assert_eq!(score_layer(&drift, Some(0), 24, false), 100);\n        assert_eq!(\n            stale_reason_for(100, 0, false, true, DriftBasis::Measured),\n            None\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn unknown_sync_age_is_unknown_not_today() {\n        assert_eq!(days_since_rfc3339(\"\"), None);\n        assert_eq!(days_since_rfc3339(\"not-a-timestamp\"), None);\n        // A date without a time/offset is not RFC 3339.\n        assert_eq!(days_since_rfc3339(\"2026-09-15\"), None);\n        assert_eq!(days_since_rfc3339(&Utc::now().to_rfc3339()), Some(0));\n        assert!(days_since_rfc3339(\"2020-01-01T00:00:00Z\").unwrap() > 100);\n\n        use crate::freshness::git::{DriftBasis, GitDrift};\n        let measured = GitDrift {\n            commits_since_baseline: 0,\n            changed_files: vec![],\n            basis: DriftBasis::Measured,\n        };\n        // Unknown age costs the saturated penalty; it must not outscore a Some(\"asset_not_ready\")\n        );\n    }\n}\n"

std::fs::create_dir_all(base.join(\"modules\"))?;\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(base.join(\"interfaces\"))?;\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(base.join(\"routes\"))?;\n
